{{2016–17 Big Ten men's basketball standings}}
The '''2016–17 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] in the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They were led by sixth-year head coach [[Mark Turgeon]] and played their home games at [[Xfinity Center (College Park, Maryland)|Xfinity Center]] in [[College Park, Maryland]] as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]].

They finished the season 24–9, 12–6 in [[2016–17 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a tie for second place. As the No. 3 seed in the [[2017 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they lost to [[2016–17 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|Northwestern]] in the quarterfinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. As a No. 6 seed in the West region, they lost in the first round to [[2016–17 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]].

==Previous season==
The [[2015–16 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Terrapins]] finished the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16 season]] with a record of 27–9, 12–6 in [[2015–16 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a four-way tie for third place in conference. They defeated [[2015–16 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2016 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] to advance to the semifinals where they lost to [[2015–16 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they defeated [[2015–16 South Dakota State Jackrabbits men's basketball team|South Dakota State]] and [[2015–16 Hawaii Rainbow Warriors basketball team|Hawaii]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen. In the Sweet Sixteen, they lost to [[2015–16 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]].
